newsitem.title: USA: HOME INSURANCE SETTLES NCCI OBLIGATION.
newsitem.headline: HOME INSURANCE SETTLES NCCI OBLIGATION.

text.p: Home Holdings Inc said its principal subsidiary, Home Insurance Co, reached an agreement to settle obligations to the National Council on Compensation Insurance, the National Workers Compensation Reinsurance Pool and the National Pool's participating companies.
Home Holdings declined to comment on the size of its obligation and how much it agreed to pay in the settlement.

But Business Insurance, a weekly trade magazine, in April said Home Insurance had offered to pay $40 million to settle total obligations of about $245 million to the residual market workers compensation pool.
Home Holdings said the terms of the settlement agreement fully release Home Insurance's obligations and will save the company $100 million.
New Hampshire insurance regulators placed Home Insurance under formal supervision in March because of concern about its capital levels.
The settlement was completed on Friday after it was approved by the New Hampshire insurance commissioner.
Additional details about the settlement were not immediately available.
Home Holdings was formerly majority owned by a unit of Trygg-Hansa AB.
